title: How Fusion Energy Finally Became Real

slides.heading: How Fusion Energy Finally Became Real
slides.body: The power of stars — now on Earth. The breakthrough that could change everything.

slides.heading: What Is Nuclear Fusion?
slides.body: Fusion is the same process that powers the Sun. Two hydrogen atoms are forced together to form helium, releasing enormous energy. Unlike fission (splitting atoms), fusion produces no long-lived radioactive waste.

slides.heading: The 60-Year Dream
slides.body: Scientists have chased fusion since the 1950s. The joke was always that commercial fusion is '30 years away — and always will be.' The extreme temperatures required (100 million°C) made sustained reactions seem impossible.

slides.heading: The NIF Breakthrough
slides.body: In December 2022, the National Ignition Facility in California achieved ignition for the first time: the fusion reaction produced more energy than the lasers put in. This milestone — called 'scientific energy gain' — rewrote the physics textbooks.

slides.heading: How Tokamaks Contain the Fire
slides.body: The most common fusion design is the tokamak — a donut-shaped chamber that uses powerful magnetic fields to contain plasma at 150 million°C. ITER, the world's largest tokamak under construction in France, will test this at full scale.

slides.heading: The Private Sector Race
slides.body: Over $6 billion in private funding has poured into fusion startups. Companies like Commonwealth Fusion, TAE Technologies, and Helion are pursuing novel designs. Helion signed a power purchase deal with Microsoft — the first commercial fusion contract ever.

slides.heading: Fuel: Seawater and Lithium
slides.body: Fusion runs on deuterium (extracted from seawater) and tritium (made from lithium). The fuel is virtually unlimited — a glass of seawater could power a home for a year. No carbon emissions, no meltdown risk, no supply chain wars.

slides.heading: The Remaining Challenges
slides.body: Sustaining reactions long enough, building materials that survive neutron bombardment, and achieving 'wall-plug efficiency' (more power out than the whole plant uses) remain unsolved. Engineering a working power plant is a massive step beyond lab ignition.

slides.heading: When Will It Power Our Homes?
slides.body: Most experts now say the 2030s–2040s for first commercial plants. Commonwealth Fusion aims for a pilot plant by 2030. If even one startup succeeds at scale, it changes the global energy equation permanently.

slides.heading: A Star in a Bottle
slides.body: Fusion isn't science fiction anymore — it's an engineering race. The question is no longer if, but when. The era of clean, limitless fusion power may arrive within our lifetime.
